title: Invocation compatibility middleware and fuzzy name resolution for tool/function interop
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers using legacy function invocation semantics and those using OpenAI-style tool calling expect different naming, parameter shapes, and streaming behaviors. This causes frequent customer friction when they migrate models or when the platform routes requests across hosted/dedicated/private environments.

Goal: Build a compatibility middleware (runtime component + policy layer) that transparently translates invocation surfaces between OpenAI-style tools and our legacy function RPCs. The middleware must: preserve semantic fidelity (arguments, return types, error provenance), support streaming partial tool outputs, apply fuzzy name resolution for function/tool name mismatches, and provide observability + audit trails for any remapping.

Scope: implementation in serving runtime and proxy layer; config-driven mapping table + heuristic resolver; fallback and safety policy; integration tests and canary rollout plan. Not in scope: changing public API for new customers — this is a backward-compatible translation layer.

Why this matters: We routinely see support tickets where small naming differences or structured output variants prevent tool calls from executing. Customers need reliable migration paths and graceful rollback when models change behavior. This component increases portability of prompts across model versions and reduces customer integration work during upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Requests that match legacy function signatures are accepted and routed to existing handlers without any change to calling code.
OpenAI-style tool calls with exact name matches route with zero-loss parameter mapping.

For name mismatches, fuzzy resolver suggests top-3 candidate mappings in logs and applies highest-confidence mapping automatically when confidence >= 0.85; otherwise request is rejected with structured diagnostic in response.
Streaming tool output is surfaced to the client as a stream of chuncks that include provenance tags indicating whether content is produced by model or a translated legacy function.
End-to-end latency overhead for successful mapped calls < 10ms P50 on dedicated pools (goal: < 5ms).
Automated test harness covers 95% of translation permutations (positional vs named args, extra optional fields, legacy enum vs new string literals).
technical_notes: Architecture: lightweight proxy module sits between the request router and the function invoker in runtime; it performs name normalization, parameter shape canonicalization, and streaming adapter duties.

Fuzzy name resolution: combination of tokenized name similarity (Jaro-Winkler on short identifiers), signature fingerprinting (parameter names/types), and historical mapping frequency (learned alias table per customer). Final confidence score is a weighted sum: 0.5 * signature_score + 0.3 * name_score + 0.2 * historical_score.

Parameter canonicalization: use a deterministic canonical type system for structured outputs; add conversion rules for legacy enums and numeric codes to modern string labels; preserve unknown fields in a metadata bag (x-legacy-extra) to ensure no data loss.

Streaming: implement a 'tool-call-stream' envelope with fields: event_type (partial|done|error), source (model|legacy), seq, payload, provenance_id. The envelope must be serializable for both chunked HTTP streaming and websocket/subscription transports.

Provenance and audit: every translated call must include headers: X-Redwood-Inference-Translation: <policy-id>, X-Translation-Confidence: <float>, X-Original-Name: <string>. These are recorded in request logs and surfaced in the Console trace view.
Security: ensure middleware does not expand surface for privilege escalation. Mappings that expose additional parameters will be rejected unless explicitly whitelisted by customer config (RBAC).
tasks: Prototype fuzzy resolver library and unit tests.
Add translation proxy to runtime code path behind feature flag.
Implement streaming envelope and update SDK clients to decode provenance tags (JS + Python).
Create conversion table for common legacy enums used by top 12 customers.
Integrate translation metadata into Console trace and create an observability dashboard.
Write regression tests for error cases and partial-streaming interruption.
Run internal canary on dedicated pool for two weeks, gather SLO/latency metrics.
Publish migration guide + example mappings in Confluence and include troubleshooting section.
comments: 2026-01-29 - Aisha Kapoor: Spike completed. Initial fuzzy resolver prototype shows >92% recall on our synthetic alias dataset but precision drops when parameter sets overlap. Need stronger signature weighting.
2026-02-10 - Miguel Alvarez: Design review notes - prefer deterministic tie-breaker rules to avoid nondeterministic routing. Add explicit mapping override facility for customers.
2026-02-22 - Dana Park (PM): Prioritize observability early; customers want to see what mapping occurred before rollout. Add console annotations to traces.

2026-02-28 - Security review (Sophie Li): flagged that metadata headers may leak PII in logs. Action: sanitize headers and only include pseudonymous translation IDs in logs; full details available in restricted audit logs.

2026-03-05 - QA: found a streaming regression where the last 'done' envelope was lost under certain backpressure scenarios. Root cause: buffer flush logic. Patch PR ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4672.
2026-03-10 - Miguel Alvarez: Ready for canary toggle. Deployed feature flag to dedicated-us-west-2 pool. Monitoring dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/translation-canary
